newsitem.title: USA: TALKING POINT - Morris poised for more gains.
newsitem.headline: TALKING POINT - Morris poised for more gains.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc stock, extending a strong rally in recent sessions, is primed for heavy gains in the short term because of sound fundamentals and the perception that regulatory threats are easing.

The resignation of U.S. Food and Drug Administration Director David Kessler, the most visible anti-tobacco crusader in recent history, has allowed the investment community to begin concentrating on tangibles -- such as sales -- and shed fears of restrictive regulations on the company's cigarette business.
Philip Morris is also one huge food company.
"With the administration's vendetta against tobacco, there was a cloud that was hanging over," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood.
"Many investors thought, 'Why buy tobacco?' With that cloud partially removed, the feeling is that the outlook is not as bad as everyone thought," Brown said.

Shares in the world's largest tobacco vendor were up 3-1/4 at 117-1/2 in late trading Tuesday on the New York Stock Exchange, edging back from a 52-week high of 118. In the previous session, Philip Morris gained 4-7/8.
The price has come a long way back from the precipitous drop that began August 9, when a Florida jury awarded the first-ever damages against a tobacco company to a smoker.

From a price of about 106, the stock plummeted to near its 52-week low of 85-5/8, carving billions of dollars of market capitalization out of the company and sending a shudder through Wall Street, which had long considered Big Tobacco impervious to investment danger.
The headlines of the past summer, which shouted litigation woes at every turn, have subsided, and no significant court dates loom until well into 1997.
Among the challenges facing the company and the rest of the industry next year is an appeal of the $750,000 award to the Florida smoker.
The industry is also at the center of a political battle that pits Mississippi Gov. Kirk Fordice, a Republican, against the state's Democratic Attorney General Mike Moore.

Moore, along with 18 other state attorneys general and several cities, is suing the tobacco industry to recoup Medicaid funds spent on the treatment of smoking-related illnesses. Fordice is trying to block Moore's suit.
Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co, said that some observers had given Philip Morris "up for dead two to three months ago, and it has suddenly rallied and is finding new life."
"It felt to me that, with a strong market and very low inflation, and no litigation until April, the stock was going to move," Salomon Brothers analyst Diana Temple said.

On December 6, Temple raised her rating of the stock -- a component of the Dow Jones Industrial Average -- to a trading buy from hold. She raised her earnings estimate for 1996 to $9.05 a share from $8.85.
The mean estimate from analysts in the First Call network forecasts profit of $1.80 a share in the fourth quarter and $7.67 for the full year.

The stock has also benefited recently from Oppenheimer & Co analyst Roy Burry reiterating his buy rating on the stock, and Goldman Sachs raising its 12-month share price target to $135 from the previous target of $125.
"It looks like it still has 10 points to go before March," Temple said, noting stronger-than-expected cigarette sales in the United States and other countries this year.
"It all depends on whether we see further slippage in litigation as to where we go from here," she said.
The projected stock price of $125 has solid prospects on a technical basis as well, said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities.

After trading in a broad range between 86 and 106 during the past year, the stock's ability to maintain its move above 106 in late November signaled a break-out that projects to 126 in the short to intermediate term of three to six months, Nie said.
"That's a solid price objective, chart-wise," Nie said, adding, "The way these stocks start cranking, that could happen quickly."
--New York Equities Desk (212) 859-1725
